description: CodeQL policy baseline. The ceiling is a RATCHET, not a budget: it records how many open findings the tree carried when it was last measured, so a new one fails and a fixed one is visible as slack to lock in.
establishedBy: RootLco CodeQL Application Remediation and Security Hardening, from the SARIF of the hosted `code-security` job on the remediation branch.
expectedLanguagesNote: A language that was not analysed cannot be reported clean. If a SARIF for either is missing the gate fails rather than judging the languages it happens to have — the AR-45 shape, where a scan that enumerated nothing read as a scan that found nothing.
maximumOpenFindingsNote: Zero OPEN findings — where open means neither dismissed by GitHub nor covered by an approved dismissal below. Every alert in the 21-alert baseline was fixed: the two application findings structurally, the fifteen script findings directly, the four vacuous assertions repaired. A ceiling above zero would be a budget for the next one. The count deliberately includes medium and low, which is how the one dismissal below was caught at all — GitHub's own CodeQL check reported that run as SUCCESS, because it blocks only on high and critical.
dismissalsNote: ZERO entries. There was exactly one — `js/http-to-file-access` at `scripts/ci/check-commit-checks.mjs`, reviewed 2026-07-29 with an expiry of 2027-01-31 — and it was REMOVED because the finding was fixed rather than allowed to expire: the script no longer writes to the filesystem at all, so there is no network-to-file edge left to adjudicate. See docs/engineering/security/codeql-remediation/sec-codeql-033-http-to-file-access.md. The gate treats a dismissal matching nothing as a lie about the tree and fails on it, which is exactly why this array had to be emptied in the same change that removed the flow. A dismissal must still name the exact rule, the exact path, a reproduction of why the source cannot be attacker-controlled AND why the sink is safe, a reviewer, a review date and an expiry; the same rule at a different path is a new finding, not a covered one; and nothing under src/ may be dismissed here at all.

dismissalSchema.ruleId: the exact CodeQL rule, e.g. js/incomplete-sanitization
dismissalSchema.path: the exact repo-relative path — dismissals are per-path on purpose
dismissalSchema.source: what the dataflow source is, and why it cannot be attacker-controlled
dismissalSchema.sink: what the sink is, and why reaching it is safe
dismissalSchema.reason: the refutation, reproducible by someone else
dismissalSchema.expiresOn: ISO date; an expired dismissal fails the gate

applicationScopeNote: Findings under src/ are APPLICATION findings and may never be dismissed by this file at all — they are fixed or refuted in code. The split is enforced by codeql-policy.mjs, which fails if a dismissal covers an application path.
